# Moodle Development Instructions

This repo follows Moodle plugin conventions. Apply the relevant skill below to any Moodle-related task.

- **moodle-5-3-changes** — Use when porting a plugin or theme to Moodle 5.3 (branch 503, MOODLE_503_STABLE, $version 2026100500), adding 5.3 to $plugin->supported or CI, or fixing what 5.3 broke or deprecated — user/lib.php functions moved to \core\user, external_* functions that now throw, FEATURE_GROUPMEMBERSONLY, set_main_table() alias, duration units, queue_adhoc_task returning an id, the sr parameter, Classic theme removal, React primary/secondary navigation, dark colour mode, theme_boost/bootstrap imports, block_timeline renderer removal, quiz report action bar, assign overrides and marker events, enablemyhome on fresh sites, delete_course async. Skip when the plugin supports only 5.2 or the port starts from a version before 5.2, or when the question is the porting method (version guards, db/upgrade.php steps, PHP versions) rather than the 5.3 list (moodle-upgrade-migration), or the task is a theme recipe rather than what changed (moodle-theme-development).
- **moodle-accessibility** — Use when building or reviewing Moodle plugin UI for WCAG 2.2 AA - semantic Mustache markup, headings and landmarks, formslib labels, {{#pix}} icon alt text and aria-hidden, accessible names for buttons, row checkboxes and icon links, ARIA only where HTML has no equivalent, live regions and core/toast, focus in core/modal and core/local/aria/focuslock, keyboard support, colour contrast in light and dark colour modes (data-bs-theme, --mds-* tokens), page titles, and the Behat axe steps ("the page should meet accessibility standards", @accessibility, --colourmode=dark, "No data"). Skip when styling a whole theme (moodle-theme-scss) or writing JavaScript mechanics (moodle-amd-javascript).
- **moodle-amd-javascript** — Use when writing or debugging JavaScript for a Moodle plugin - amd/src ES modules and the amd/build output, `grunt amd`, `js_call_amd()`, core/ajax, core/str, core/templates, core/modal and ModalEvents, core/notification and core/toast, core/pending for Behat, core/fragment, core/form-autocomplete ajax handlers, TinyMCE (editor_tiny) plugins, localStorage, Bootstrap imports, 5.3 core/import and React mounting, or errors such as "No define call for", "is not a function" on `.finally`, a named import that is undefined, "Too much data passed as arguments to js_call_amd", "The theme has already been set up". Skip when the work is server-side only (moodle-web-services for external functions) or theme-wide styling (moodle-theme-scss).
- **moodle-behat-testing** — Use when writing, running or debugging Behat acceptance tests for a Moodle plugin - tests/behat/*.feature, behat_<component>.php step definitions, tests/generator/behat_<component>_generator.php and the "the following ... exist" step, public/admin/tool/behat/cli/init.php and run.php, @javascript scenarios, --scss-deprecations, "Deprecated style in use", "Deprecated styles found", gherkinlint failures in moodle-plugin-ci grunt, "I set the field" matching the wrong field, "I should not see" passing for the wrong reason, a new feature or step not being picked up, faildumps, or user tours blocking clicks. Covers the Behat site's mental model, the default feature and step recipe, and locator and assertion traps. Skip when testing business logic without a browser (moodle-phpunit-testing), building the CI workflow (moodle-ci-matrix), writing or fixing the axe accessibility steps (moodle-accessibility), or running a theme's own suite (moodle-theme-testing-release).
- **moodle-ci-matrix** — Use when adding or updating a GitHub Actions workflow that runs moodle-plugin-ci for a Moodle plugin (.github/workflows/ci.yml from gha.dist.yml), choosing its Moodle branch x PHP x database matrix, or when CI fails at "Initialize containers", at moodle-plugin-ci install, with "requires at least PHP", an empty DB in a job, an artifact-name error, "No PHPUnit tests to run, free pass!", or green while the Plugins directory still rejects the plugin. Covers the upstream template and its steps, reading each branch's environment.xml and core push.yml, service image pins and health checks, include/exclude pitfalls, non-blocking rows for main, running the pipeline locally as written, secrets in logs, optional PHP extensions, and what a green run does not check. Skip when running PHPUnit or Behat locally with no workflow involved (moodle-phpunit-testing, moodle-behat-testing) or for theme-specific CI (moodle-theme-testing-release).
- **moodle-definition-of-done** — Use when about to report a Moodle plugin or theme task complete, open a pull request, or hand work over for review. A definition-of-done checklist covering the moodle-plugin-ci gates (phplint, phpcs, phpdoc/moodlecheck, validate, savepoints, mustache, grunt with eslint, stylelint and gherkinlint), reading gate output instead of piping it through tail, PHPUnit and Behat counts, install.xml and upgrade path, course lifecycle (backup, restore, reset, uninstall and user preferences), privacy provider coverage, lang strings, renames, installing on a real site with upgrade and cache purge, browser checks in Firefox and Chromium as each role, CSS evidence, and proving each check can fail. Skip when exploring or prototyping with no intent to ship, when the next step is a tag or a Plugins directory submission (moodle-release-preflight, then moodle-plugin-release), or for theme-only checks such as SCSS compile, dark mode and RTL (moodle-theme-testing-release).
- **moodle-field-lessons** — Use when scanning a Moodle plugin change across topics for the non-obvious pitfalls that pass phpcs, PHPUnit and CI but break on a real site, or when a symptom fits no single topic skill - a short-rule index by topic: supported ranges and cross-branch guards, functions or classes missing outside PHPUnit, client-supplied ids, html_writer and format_string escaping, noclean under "Log in as", DB and XMLDB small print, backup/restore/reset date shifts across DST, privacy drift, lang placeholders and [[key]], moodleform/dynamic_form/file picker traps, admin settings defaults, the question engine outside mod_quiz, availability conditions, core AI calls, modal and TinyMCE gotchas, navigation and course-page content, and CI false greens. Skip when the task sits inside one topic and you need its recipe, checklist or error message explained (that topic's skill, such as moodle-plugin-development or moodle-security-audit), before a release (moodle-release-preflight), or for a theme (the moodle-theme-* skills).
- **moodle-hooks-api** — Use when a plugin listens to or dispatches a Moodle hook — db/hooks.php, \core\hook\manager, \core\di, hook classes under classes/hook/, replacing lib.php callbacks such as before_http_headers, before_footer, before_standard_html_head, before_standard_top_of_body_html, add_htmlattributes, after_config or bulk_user_actions, the debugging message "Callback ... should be migrated to new hook callback", extend_user_menu, primary_extend, secondary_extend, or testing hook callbacks with phpunit_get_instance. Skip when reacting to a logged fact with \core\event observers (moodle-plugin-development), or when choosing where a theme puts page markup (moodle-theme-renderers-output).
- **moodle-language-pack** — Use when asked to translate a Moodle plugin's strings into another language, "add a language pack" (es, ja, pt_br, zh_tw ...), update an existing translation after lang/en changed, or try a translation on a test site. Covers the file name per plugin type (lang/<code>/<component>.php, an activity's <modname>.php), Moodle's language codes, keeping every key and only the keys of lang/en, placeholders ({$a}, {$a->name}) and HTML kept intact, _help strings, PHP quoting, checking a pack with php -l and a key and placeholder diff, keeping packs outside the plugin repository (the package ships lang/en only), installing a pack as a local customisation (<code>_local under $CFG->langlocalroot) to view it with ?lang=, and contributing it through AMOS. Skip when adding or renaming English strings (moodle-plugin-development) or finding hard-coded English (the /moodle-string-check command).
- **moodle-marketplace-package** — Use when asked to prepare a Moodle Plugins directory (Marketplace) submission or listing update - "make the Marketplace package", "publishing docs", listing text, screenshots for the plugin page. Produces one folder per release with listing.txt (every form field ready to paste: name, type, component, short description, full description as HTML, source control URL, bug tracker URL, documentation URL, supported versions, maturity, release notes, screenshot captions), listing.md (where each claim and screenshot came from), the numbered screenshots and the release ZIP. Covers reading the field values from version.php, the git remote and the README, checking the issue tracker is enabled, writing descriptions that make only checked claims, and taking listing screenshots. Skip when building the ZIP, tagging or answering a reviewer (moodle-plugin-release), auditing the code before release (moodle-release-preflight), or making an internal walkthrough report (moodle-walkthrough).
- **moodle-mobile-app** — Use when adding Moodle app (mobile) support to a plugin - db/mobile.php handlers and delegates (CoreMainMenuDelegate, CoreCourseModuleDelegate, CoreCourseOptionsDelegate, CoreBlockDelegate, CoreQuestionDelegate), classes/output/mobile.php methods called through tool_mobile_get_content, templates/mobileapp Mustache with {{=<% %>=}} and Ionic markup, otherdata and CONTENT_OTHERDATA, core-site-plugins-call-ws and other site-plugin directives, handler JavaScript (this.CoreSitesProvider, updateContent caching, detectChanges), offlinefunctions and prefetch, app CSS (--ion-*-color-step-N, :root.dark), push notifications, and errors such as "Scalar type expected, array or object received", "Access control exception", "serverconnectionajax" or a plugin that silently does nothing in the app. Skip when the plugin has no app UI and only needs web services (moodle-web-services).
- **moodle-performance** — Use when a Moodle page, web service, filter or task is slow, runs too many queries, or runs out of memory, or when adding caching or background work - db/caches.php and \core_cache\cache::make (MUC application, session and request caches, cachedef_ strings, invalidation events), per-context or per-call repeated queries, N+1 loops, get_recordset vs get_records, batching large tables, $DB->perf_get_queries() budgets, ad-hoc and scheduled tasks (db/tasks.php, queue_adhoc_task, locks, retries), session locks, perfdebug, profiling and server tuning. Skip when the slowness is theme CSS compilation (moodle-theme-scss) or the task is a schema change (moodle-plugin-development).
- **moodle-phpunit-testing** — Use when writing, running or debugging PHPUnit tests for a Moodle plugin or core - tests/*_test.php, advanced_testcase, resetAfterTest, data generators (tests/generator/lib.php), public/admin/tool/phpunit/cli/init.php and util.php, vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite, "No tests executed!", "Unexpected debugging() call detected", "unexpected database modification", tests that pass on MySQL or MariaDB and fail on PostgreSQL, preventResetByRollback, redirectEvents/redirectMessages/redirectEmails, external functions with clean_returnvalue, route_testcase, privacy provider tests, mock_clock_with_frozen and get_mocked_http_client. Covers the test framework's mental model, the default test recipe, invocation traps, fixture and database traps from shipped plugins, and pointers to generators, special test cases and PostgreSQL isolation. Skip when writing Behat acceptance tests (moodle-behat-testing) or building a CI workflow (moodle-ci-matrix).
- **moodle-plugin-development** — Use when creating, modifying or reviewing any Moodle plugin (local, mod, block, format, auth, enrol, report, tool, qtype, filter, repository, tiny, availability, sub-plugins) - version.php ($plugin->version, requires, supported), db/install.xml and db/upgrade.php, db/access.php capabilities, db/services.php, db/tasks.php, db/caches.php, lang/en strings, classes/ autoloading and frankenstyle names, lib.php callbacks versus hooks, settings.php, page scripts (require_login, require_capability, sesskey, PARAM types), privacy provider, the LICENSE file, "No upgrade needed" after a db/ change, "Incorrect syntax in plugin supported declaration". Skip when the plugin is a theme (moodle-theme-development), the task is porting to another Moodle version (moodle-upgrade-migration, moodle-5-3-changes) or releasing (moodle-plugin-release), or you want the cross-topic pitfall index (moodle-field-lessons).
- **moodle-plugin-release** — Use when releasing a Moodle plugin or theme, or submitting it to the Moodle Plugins directory (Marketplace): bumping $plugin->version vs $plugin->release, CHANGES.md and changelog entries, the LICENSE file and ZIP root folder a reviewer checks, building and listing the ZIP before upload (rootdirinvalid, "Missing plugin license file", "Use the plugin folder name as the root folder of the ZIP"), staging and tagging an annotated vX.Y.Z, pushing the branch before the tag, the moodle-release.yml workflow, replying to a Plugins directory reviewer's issue, and confirming the version landed. Skip when only bumping version for a schema change (the /moodle-bump-version command) finishing the change itself (moodle-definition-of-done), or auditing the code for what reviewers catch (moodle-release-preflight).
- **moodle-privacy-gdpr** — Use when writing, reviewing or testing a Moodle plugin's privacy provider (classes/privacy/provider.php), adding a table, user preference, file area or external API call that holds personal data, or when the Plugin privacy registry says "Requires attention" or "Userlist provider missing". Covers null_provider vs metadata provider plus request\plugin\provider, get_metadata (add_database_table, add_subsystem_link, add_external_location_link, add_user_preference), get_contexts_for_userid, get_users_in_context, export_user_data, delete_data_for_all_users_in_context, delete_data_for_user, delete_data_for_users, core_userlist_provider, user_preference_provider, exporting and deleting files, comments, ratings and tags through core's helpers, activity and subplugin providers, and provider_testcase tests. Skip when auditing request handling for security (moodle-security-audit), running the whole pre-release audit (moodle-release-preflight), or declaring a theme's user preferences (moodle-theme-settings).
- **moodle-release-preflight** — Use when about to tag a Moodle plugin release, submit it to the Moodle Plugins directory, fix a code finding a Plugins directory reviewer raised, or send the plugin for an external security review. A pre-release audit of the defect classes reviews caught in shipped plugins despite green CI: client-trusted ids and limits, require_login() without a capability, sibling actions that skip a rule, frozen form fields, unescaped output sinks, inline-served uploads, unclean restore and imports, settings read by name, privacy drift, reset and uninstall gaps, vacuous tests, missing frankenstyle prefixes, missing lang strings, PARAM_RAW, mkdir 0777, raw cURL, and an extended checklist (unserialize, IDOR, CSRF, noclean, SSRF, group leaks). Skip when writing new feature code (moodle-plugin-development), reviewing code for security with no release at stake (moodle-security-audit), finishing an ordinary task (moodle-definition-of-done), or building the ZIP, tagging and replying to the reviewer (moodle-plugin-release).
- **moodle-security-audit** — Use when reviewing or hardening Moodle plugin code for security, auditing a plugin's entry points, or responding to a vulnerability report. Covers require_login and require_capability, IDOR (context derived from the record), sesskey and CSRF, required_param and PARAM_* types, $DB placeholders and get_in_or_equal, output escaping (s, format_string, format_text, html_writer, Mustache triple braces, JS sinks), pluginfile and send_stored_file, uploads, \curl and SSRF, open redirects (PARAM_LOCALURL), secrets and \core\encryption, external functions (validate_context), dynamic forms, mobile methods and tasks. Skip when the audit is the gate before a tag, a Plugins directory submission or a reviewer's finding (moodle-release-preflight).
- **moodle-theme-boost-child** — Use when building or fixing a Moodle theme whose config.php has $THEME->parents = ['boost'] (a Boost child) or ['boost_union', 'boost'] (a grandchild) - the minimal config.php, lib.php, version.php and lang file, which $THEME keys must be restated (rendererfactory, haseditswitch, usescourseindex, requiredblocks), theme_boost_get_main_scss_content and presets, why brandcolor, scsspre or the background image is ignored, a child that lost the edit switch, the course index or its renderer overrides, screenshot, favicon and the null privacy provider, and what breaks when Boost changes between 5.2 and 5.3. Skip when the question is the SCSS itself or a theme that renders as plain Boost (moodle-theme-scss), layouts or templates (moodle-theme-layouts-templates), renderers or hooks (moodle-theme-renderers-output), the settings page (moodle-theme-settings), or choosing between a child and a stand-alone theme (moodle-theme-development).
- **moodle-theme-development** — Use when starting, structuring or debugging a Moodle theme at the engine level - a new theme/<name>/ directory, config.php and the $THEME keys, version.php and theme dependencies, $THEME->parents and what a child inherits, which theme a page uses (allowcoursethemes, allowthemechangeonurl and ?theme=, $CFG->themeorder), theme caches (themerev, theme designer mode, purge_caches.php, build_theme_css.php), "my change does not show" after a purge, "theme cannot be initialised", a theme problem whose area is not yet known, or choosing between a Boost child, a grandchild and a stand-alone theme. Also the routing table to the six sibling theme skills. Skip when the task is already inside one area: Boost child files (moodle-theme-boost-child), SCSS or a theme that renders as plain Boost (moodle-theme-scss), layouts and templates (moodle-theme-layouts-templates), renderers (moodle-theme-renderers-output), settings (moodle-theme-settings), testing and release (moodle-theme-testing-release).
- **moodle-theme-layouts-templates** — Use when changing page structure in a Moodle theme - $THEME->layouts, layout/*.php files, block regions, layout options, copying Boost's drawers.php or drawers.mustache, overriding Mustache templates under templates/<component>/, the "!" include, drawers and the course index, body classes, the maintenance, secure and login layouts, or working out which 5.3 navigation parts are React-rendered; also for "Can not find layout file", "does not contain the main content placeholder", a filenotfound error on core/secondarymoremenu, or a template override that is ignored. Skip when the change is CSS only (moodle-theme-scss), a PHP renderer or React component override (moodle-theme-renderers-output), or the theme's config and caches (moodle-theme-development).
- **moodle-theme-renderers-output** — Use when a Moodle theme changes output in PHP — $THEME->rendererfactory, theme_overridden_renderer_factory, classes/output/core_renderer.php, plugin renderer overrides, a theme's db/hooks.php callbacks, $THEME->iconsystem, get_fontawesome_icon_map, pix_core and pix_plugins, $THEME->activityheaderconfig, $THEME->removedprimarynavitems, primary navigation data, or a React component override in js/esm/src/overrides (5.3). Skip when the change is a Mustache or layout file (moodle-theme-layouts-templates), SCSS (moodle-theme-scss) or a settings page (moodle-theme-settings).
- **moodle-theme-scss** — Use when writing or debugging a Moodle theme's SCSS or CSS - `$THEME->scss`, `prescsscallback` / `extrascsscallback`, pre.scss and post.scss, `@import` paths that must work on 5.2 and 5.3, Bootstrap variables and `!default`, `--bs-*` / `--mds-*` custom properties and design tokens, dark mode (`data-bs-theme`), re-branding, presets, fonts, `[[pix:]]` / `[[font:]]`, RTL directives, editor SCSS, stylelint, or when a theme renders as plain Boost ("Error while compiling SCSS", "file not found for @import"). Skip when the task is theme structure or caches (moodle-theme-development), layouts or templates (moodle-theme-layouts-templates), renderers or icons (moodle-theme-renderers-output), the settings page (moodle-theme-settings), proving the styles with tests (moodle-theme-testing-release), or contrast and markup rules for a plugin page (moodle-accessibility).
- **moodle-theme-settings** — Use when adding or fixing a Moodle theme's admin settings - theme settings.php, themesetting<name> section, theme_boost_admin_settingspage_tabs, admin_setting_configcolourpicker, admin_setting_configstoredfile, admin_setting_scsscode, hide_if, set_updatedcallback('theme_reset_all_caches'), $theme->settings versus get_config('theme_x'), setting to SCSS variable, setting to template context, setting_file_url / setting_file_serve / theme_x_pluginfile, renaming settings in db/upgrade.php, theme user preferences and the privacy provider that declares them; symptoms such as "Section error" from the theme selector cog, a saved setting that changes nothing, a 404 logo, or stock Boost styling after saving a setting. Skip when the task is the SCSS itself (moodle-theme-scss), layouts or templates (moodle-theme-layouts-templates), or settings of a non-theme plugin (moodle-plugin-development).
- **moodle-theme-testing-release** — Use when testing, linting, packaging or submitting a Moodle theme - a PHPUnit test that compiles the theme, the theme's own Behat suite (--suite=<theme>, @theme_<name> tags, behat_theme_<name>_behat_*.php overrides, blacklist.json), computed-style and axe checks, dark mode (--colourmode, 5.3) and RTL checks, --scss-deprecations, stylelint and Mustache lint of overridden core templates, moodle-plugin-ci for themes, and Plugins directory rules for themes (LICENSE file, ZIP root folder, screenshot, choosereadme, thirdpartylibs.xml for fonts); also for "0 scenarios" from a theme feature, a core feature that fails only under the theme, or CI that stays green while the theme's SCSS does not compile. Skip when writing the theme itself (start at moodle-theme-development), for Behat, PHPUnit, CI and release mechanics that are not theme-specific (moodle-behat-testing, moodle-phpunit-testing, moodle-ci-matrix, moodle-plugin-release), or for the axe steps (moodle-accessibility).
- **moodle-upgrade-migration** — Use when porting a Moodle plugin written for 3.x, 4.x, 5.0 or 5.1 up to 5.2, moving it to a newer PHP version, or needing the porting method for any version: raising $plugin->requires and $plugin->supported, one codebase or a branch per Moodle version, guarding an API that differs between supported branches, fixing deprecation debugging ("has been deprecated", "Call to undefined function print_error", "Undefined constant"), writing db/upgrade.php steps that must survive a failed upgrade, or porting old code (print_error, add_to_log, external_api without namespace, lib.php callbacks, Bootstrap 4 classes, /public directory). Skip when the question is what Moodle 5.3 removed, moved, deprecated or added (moodle-5-3-changes) or writing a plugin from scratch (moodle-plugin-development).
- **moodle-walkthrough** — Use when asked to "make the walkthrough", walk through a Moodle plugin or theme on a real site, or produce screenshots and a report (usually a PDF) of what each role sees. Covers listing what to cover from the code, deploying and checking the installed version, demo courses and users made for the walkthrough, driving Chromium and Firefox with Playwright as each role at desktop and phone width, user tours and drawers that spoil shots, reading every screenshot before using it, separating plugin problems from harness problems, the report's structure, keeping the Markdown source beside the PDF with relative image links, rendering the PDF and checking it. Skip when writing automated acceptance tests (moodle-behat-testing), checking a task before calling it done (moodle-definition-of-done), or preparing a Plugins directory listing and its screenshots (moodle-marketplace-package).
- **moodle-web-services** — Use when adding, changing, calling or debugging a Moodle external function or web service - db/services.php, classes/external/, execute_parameters/execute_returns, validate_parameters, validate_context, 'ajax' => true for core/ajax, 'loginrequired' => false, readonlysession, REST/SOAP tokens, login/token.php, webservice/upload.php, pluginfile URLs for token clients, or errors such as "Invalid parameter value detected", "Invalid response value detected", servicenotavailable, servicerequireslogin, accessexception, a function missing from external_functions. Skip when writing the JavaScript caller (moodle-amd-javascript) or the Moodle app integration (moodle-mobile-app).
